topStories.headline: Man Shot and Killed at Hunters Point Waterfront; Homicide Investigation Underway
topStories.dek: A 44-year-old man died Thursday evening after being shot on Thomas Avenue near the Yosemite Slough — the fourth homicide in Bayview so far this year.
topStories.body:
A man was shot and killed on Thursday evening in Hunters Point in what may become San Francisco's 19th homicide of the year. Officers responded to reports of gunfire on Thomas Avenue — a largely industrial street lined by warehouses at the edge of the Yosemite Slough near the South Basin waterfront — at 5:11 p.m.

The victim, described in the San Francisco Police Department's incident log as Hispanic and 44 years old, was transported to San Francisco General Hospital, where he later died from his injuries. The SFPD Homicide unit has taken over the investigation. As of Friday morning, no arrests had been made; the department's daily crime report listed two white males between the ages of 35 and 40 as suspects.

If officially classified as a homicide, the killing would be the fourth in Bayview this year — a two-fold increase over the same period last year, when the neighborhood recorded a historic low in homicides. The surge has renewed concern among residents and community advocates about public safety along the southeastern waterfront, where industrial isolation makes witnesses scarce.

topStories.headline: D10 Race: Ellington Alone on Lurie Charter Reforms as Forum Exposes Fault Lines
topStories.dek: At a September 30 candidate forum at the Southeast Community Center, frontrunner Theo Ellington was the only one of six participants to support Mayor Lurie's proposed charter amendments — a position that drew audible surprise from the crowd.
topStories.body:
The race to succeed termed-out District 10 Supervisor Shamann Walton entered its final stretch this week with a forum that sharpened contrasts among the leading candidates. At a youth-led forum held Wednesday, September 30, at the Southeast Community Center — co-hosted by Chinese for Affirmative Action and 3rd Street Youth Center & Clinic — frontrunner Theo Ellington found himself alone in supporting Mayor Daniel Lurie's proposed city charter amendments, which appear on the November ballot as Propositions D, E, and F.

When asked in a lightning-round paddle vote whether they backed the reforms, Ellington raised the green side while all five other candidates present raised red. The amendments would expand the mayor's powers and make it harder to place measures on the ballot by citizen initiative. After the forum, Ellington told the SF Standard that he believes in partnering with the mayor and city department heads for the benefit of the neighborhood.

Ellington also drew a reaction from the audience that evening by indicating he would not vote to renew the SFPD's contract with Flock, the license-plate reader system under national scrutiny, and that he would support an all-out ban on data centers. The forum came days after cryptocurrency billionaire Chris Larsen donated $500,000 to a PAC supporting Ellington — described as among the largest single contributions in the history of a San Francisco supervisorial race. Ellington's campaign committee has separately raised approximately $488,000, far ahead of rivals DJ Brookter and J.R. Eppler. The November 3 general election will decide who represents Bayview–Hunters Point, Visitacion Valley, Potrero Hill, and surrounding neighborhoods.

topStories.headline: Yvonne's Southern Sweets Marks 20 Years on Third Street With a Saturday Celebration
topStories.dek: The beloved Bayview bakery — which only recently reopened after an eight-month closure due to illness — throws a free anniversary party on October 4.
topStories.body:
Yvonne's Southern Sweets, the Third Street bakery that has been a fixture of the Bayview–Hunters Point community since owner Yvonne Hines opened its storefront in 2006, is celebrating its 20th anniversary this Saturday, October 4. The free celebration runs from 1 p.m. to 4 p.m. at the bakery at 5128 Third St.

The anniversary comes after a particularly difficult stretch for the shop. Hines announced in early February that she would close temporarily while she recovered from an illness, leaving the storefront shuttered for eight months. She returned to Instagram in mid-September to announce the reopening, initially offering limited Wednesday hours from noon to 4 p.m.

Hines, who was born and raised in Bayview–Hunters Point, began selling pralines and Southern sweets at Bay Area street festivals before opening the Third Street storefront in 2006. The business has earned recognition from the San Francisco Board of Supervisors, the California State Assembly, and Congresswoman Nancy Pelosi, and has served as a vendor for the Warriors' Chase Center. It has weathered a fire at a neighboring building in January 2025 and subsequent vandalism — each time returning to the community that has sustained it for two decades.

moreNews.headline: T-Third Overnight Maintenance Continues Through October on Bayview and Visitacion Valley Platforms
moreNews.body: SFMTA crews are conducting overnight maintenance on the T-Third light-rail line from midnight to 5 a.m. several nights per week through October 2026, covering platforms from Evans Avenue to Sunnydale. The work — announced in September — is part of a new regular maintenance program the agency established following the two-weekend 'Fix It!' shutdown of the line in July, the first major overhaul since the T-Third opened in 2007. Daytime service is unaffected; riders traveling after midnight should check the SFMTA website for platform-specific schedules.

moreNews.headline: Bayview's First New Pharmacy in More Than a Year Targets Early 2027 Opening at 5668 Third St.
moreNews.body: After the neighborhood's last Walgreens closed in February 2025, leaving nearly 35,000 Bayview–Hunters Point residents without a local pharmacy, a nonprofit replacement is moving forward. The D10 Community Pharmacy received a storefront opportunity grant from the city's Office of Economic and Workforce Development and is slated to open at 5668 Third St. — the former site of the long-closed What's the Scoop ice cream shop — with an expected opening in early 2027. The effort is led by Bayview Senior Services' Cathy Davis and Geoffrea Morris, who also launched the D10 Community Market, a free grocery store for low-income residents that opened in 2024. The pharmacy's Third Street location was chosen for its proximity to three senior housing developments and its accessibility via the Bayview Shuttle.

restaurants.name: Old Skool Cafe
restaurants.description: A 1920s speakeasy-themed supper club run by at-risk and formerly incarcerated youth, serving global soul food and live jazz every night it's open.

restaurants.name: Gumbo Social
restaurants.description: Chef Dontaye Ball's Bayview brick-and-mortar serves acclaimed build-your-own gumbo, po'boys, and smoked meats; recently reopened after a six-week retooling.

restaurants.name: All Good Pizza
restaurants.description: A beloved outdoor pizza spot in a sun-drenched garden, serving thin-crust Neapolitan pies made with organic, locally sourced ingredients; open Tuesday–Saturday.

restaurants.name: Gratta Wines
restaurants.type: Urban winery, wine bar & Italian market
restaurants.description: San Francisco's last mainland urban winery, founded in 2006 by Barbara Gratta, offering Dry Creek Valley wines, Italian small bites, and a specialty market on Third Street.

restaurants.name: Cafe Alma
restaurants.description: A welcoming community café on Third Street in the Bayview, serving coffee, food, and hosting local events and creative workshops.

restaurants.name: Beep's Burgers
restaurants.description: An Ocean Avenue institution since 1962, serving juicy burgers, curly fries, legendary garlic fries, and milkshakes at a retro drive-in counter open daily until 2 a.m.

restaurants.name: Ocean Ale House
restaurants.description: Ingleside's social anchor at 1314 Ocean Avenue, with rotating craft beers on tap, pub food, a small live-music stage, open mic nights, and a welcoming all-ages atmosphere.

restaurants.name: Megan's Table
restaurants.description: A family-run café on Ocean Avenue serving Thai and Cambodian dishes including cha kroeung, papaya salad, pad see ew, and Tom Kha soup in a warm, plant-filled setting.

restaurants.name: Pho Golden
restaurants.description: A casual Excelsior Vietnamese restaurant well-regarded for its pho and dishes featuring grilled pork.

restaurants.name: Calabria Brothers
restaurants.description: An Excelsior Italian deli counter known for oversized, generously filled sandwiches made to order.

restaurants.name: Restaurante Familiar
restaurants.description: An Excelsior neighborhood staple serving Salvadoran and Mexican fare with praised entrees at family-friendly prices.

restaurants.name: Los Planes de Renderos
restaurants.description: A popular Excelsior Salvadoran spot focused on pupusas and traditional Central American comfort food.

restaurants.name: Don Chuy's
restaurants.description: A beloved Excelsior corner store recognized for its outstanding carnitas burrito.

restaurants.name: 7 Mile House
restaurants.description: A Visitacion Valley landmark at Bayshore Boulevard and Geneva Avenue, one of San Francisco's oldest continuously operating bars, still serving drinks on the same corner for generations.

restaurants.name: Pakwan
restaurants.description: A reliable Ocean Avenue spot for tandoori chicken, chicken achar, and hearty Pakistani and Indian dishes served in generous portions.

shops.name: SCRAP (Scroungers' Center for Reusable Art Parts)
shops.description: San Francisco's beloved 50-year-old nonprofit creative reuse depot, now in a permanent new home at 141 Industrial Street — five times the size of its former warehouse — selling donated materials at low cost to artists, teachers, and makers.

shops.name: Flora Grubb Gardens
shops.description: A beloved open-air destination garden center at 1634 Jerrold Avenue in the Bayview, widely regarded as one of the finest plant shops in the Bay Area.

shops.name: Meizzei Hardware
shops.description: A legacy hardware store on the Third Street corridor that has served the Bayview community for decades.

shops.name: Ocean Subs
shops.description: An Excelsior lunch staple praised for its Original Sub on toasted Dutch crunch, stacked with Italian meats and a tangy herb vinaigrette.

artEntertainment.name: Ruth Williams Opera House (Bayview Opera House)
artEntertainment.type: Historic performing arts and cultural center
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's oldest extant theater and Landmark #8, the Ruth Williams Opera House is the cultural anchor of Bayview–Hunters Point, hosting concerts, theater, Stoop Sessions, community events, and youth arts programs.

artEntertainment.name: Jerry Garcia Amphitheater
artEntertainment.description: A free outdoor amphitheater named for the late Grateful Dead frontman, set within McLaren Park and hosting summer concerts and community performances.
artEntertainment.address: 100 John F. Shelley Dr, McLaren Park

artEntertainment.name: Quesada Gardens
artEntertainment.description: A vibrant community-built gathering space at Quesada Avenue and Newhall Street, transformed since 2006 with greenery, colorful murals, and tiled stairs.

gymsRecreation.name: Excelsior Yoga
gymsRecreation.description: A boutique Excelsior studio on the third floor of the US Bank Building on Mission Street, offering classical 90-minute Hatha yoga classes blended with science, pranayama, and meditation.

gymsRecreation.name: John McLaren Park
gymsRecreation.description: San Francisco's second-largest park, spanning Visitacion Valley and the Excelsior with over seven miles of trails, a swimming pool, tennis and basketball courts, a golf course, soccer fields, playgrounds, and the Jerry Garcia Amphitheater.

gymsRecreation.name: Crocker Amazon Playground
gymsRecreation.description: A large southern San Francisco park featuring a skate park, lighted soccer fields, basketball and tennis courts, children's play areas, and baseball and softball fields currently in a renovation planning process.

gymsRecreation.name: India Basin Shoreline Park
gymsRecreation.description: A newly developed waterfront park on the Bayview shore offering San Francisco Bay views, restored native habitat, and public shoreline access.
